collection: NECO BECE Cultural and Creative Arts JSS 3 original objective practice
note: Original classroom objective practice. Historical topic mapping and four-option format are provisional. Current NECO objectives, practical requirements and curriculum adoption remain unverified.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Choose lettering that supports clear communication.
questions.prompt: A pupil designs a notice for a school art exhibition. The title uses complicated overlapping letters that visitors struggle to read. Which change would best improve communication?
options: Use simpler letter shapes with clear spacing.
Add more overlapping letters.
Make the title the same colour as the background.
Remove every space between words.
questions.answer: Use simpler letter shapes with clear spacing.
questions.explanation: Simple shapes and clear spacing improve legibility.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise how spacing affects the reading of a caption.
questions.prompt: On a display label, the words “ART CLUB” appear as “ARTC LUB” because of uneven spaces. What should the designer correct first?
options: The number of objects in the exhibition.
The spacing within and between the words.
The material used to build the display table.
The date on the artist’s notebook.
questions.answer: The spacing within and between the words.
questions.explanation: The misplaced gaps break the intended word groups.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select a display method that supports and protects an artwork.
questions.prompt: A drawing on thin paper curls at the edges when placed on an exhibition board. Which preparation would best support a neat display?
options: Fold the drawing through its centre.
Place a wet cloth over the drawing.
Mount it securely on suitable backing.
Attach it by one loose corner only.
questions.answer: Mount it securely on suitable backing.
questions.explanation: Suitable backing supports thin paper and helps keep the work flat.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Choose placement that makes an artwork accessible to viewers.
questions.prompt: A small framed drawing is hung so high that most pupils cannot see its details. Which adjustment best serves the audience?
options: Move it behind a closed cupboard.
Place a larger label over the drawing.
Turn the drawing towards the wall.
Lower it to a comfortable viewing height.
questions.answer: Lower it to a comfortable viewing height.
questions.explanation: Placement should enable the intended viewers to see the work.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify music used to support learning.
questions.prompt: A teacher sets the steps of a classroom routine to a short song so that pupils can recall them. Which use of music is most directly shown?
options: Education.
Storage of instruments.
Repair of furniture.
Framing of pictures.
questions.explanation: The song helps pupils learn and remember a sequence.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise the persuasive use of a musical message.
questions.prompt: A radio advertisement repeats a shop’s name in a short, memorable tune. Why is music being used in this message?
options: To keep the shop’s name secret.
To help listeners remember the shop.
To replace every spoken language in the community.
To show how to repair the radio.
questions.answer: To help listeners remember the shop.
questions.explanation: A memorable tune can reinforce the name in an advertisement.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Connect a dramatic story to a specific community concern.
questions.prompt: A youth group wants a short play to encourage proper use of a shared refuse collection point. Which storyline best supports this purpose?
options: A traveller buys a hat without meeting anyone.
Two friends discuss a football result with no link to the community.
Neighbours face problems caused by dumped waste and agree on better disposal.
A performer reads a list of unrelated shop prices.
questions.answer: Neighbours face problems caused by dumped waste and agree on better disposal.
questions.explanation: The storyline connects a local problem with collective action relevant to the message.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Choose follow-up that connects a performance to practical discussion.
questions.prompt: After a play about a neglected community space, the actors invite the audience to discuss possible improvements. What is the main value of this invitation?
options: It proves that every proposal will succeed.
It removes the need to listen to residents.
It guarantees that the actors can fund every project.
It helps residents connect the drama with actions they can consider.
questions.answer: It helps residents connect the drama with actions they can consider.
questions.explanation: Discussion can help the audience relate the dramatic issue to practical choices.
